text: Rohan, Month 6 begins. Endurance increases to three sessions per week. Two sessions will remain steady zone-2. The third will include short intervals at higher intensity.
How intense should these intervals be? I don't want to overdo it.
Intervals will be 30-second zone-4 bursts with 2 minutes of zone-2 recovery. Start with 4 rounds, once per week. Keep strength sessions unchanged.
Completed the first interval session this morning. HR spiked to 150 bpm during the bursts. Felt challenging but manageable.
That's exactly the target range. Track recovery closely this week. Intervals are a new stressor, so HRV may dip temporarily.
HRV has averaged 57ms over the last 3 days, slightly down from baseline. Sleep has been 6.5 hours on average.
That's within expected range. Keep one day of full rest this week. We'll see if HRV rebounds toward 60ms.
Took a rest day yesterday. HRV today was 61ms, recovery 64%.
Great. Shows you're adapting. This balance of stress and recovery is exactly what improves long-term cardiovascular health.
This week, let's add a cognitive routine: 10 minutes of dual-tasking exercises after cardio — memory recall while walking. We want to measure endurance impact on focus.
Interesting. I'll give it a try after tomorrow's cardio session.
Tried the memory recall after cardio today. Felt sharper mentally, although more fatigued physically.
That's the desired crossover. Endurance training often improves cognitive resilience when paired with mental load. We'll track this regularly.
BP this week is averaging 122/76. HRV stable at 59-61ms. Energy feels steady despite higher training load.
That's a strong adaptation. BP is well controlled and HRV is healthy despite intervals. Excellent sign of resilience.

Month 6 summary: you've adapted to three endurance sessions, including intervals. Cognitive work is integrated. Next month we'll prepare you for a structured stress test to measure cardiovascular gains.
Understood. I feel stronger and sharper. Looking forward to seeing the test results.
